extracted.intended_audience: governments, civil society organizations, and development practitioners working on open government and SDG implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how Open Government Partnership (OGP) principles and national OGP commitments can support implementation, monitoring, and accountability for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open government principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles of transparency, civic participation, accountable public institutions, and technological innovation—core tenets of the OGP that should guide governance and SDG implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes these principles are central to OGP and are incorporated into the 2030 Agenda in multiple ways. Use these principles as foundational design criteria for commitments, action plans, and monitoring systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with SDG 16 (effective, accountable, inclusive institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open government principles are explicitly addressed in Goal 16, which aims to 'build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific language of SDG targets to justify and shape open-government reforms; treat open and responsive government as an objective in its own right rather than only an instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding open government across other SDGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency, public participation and accountable public institutions are instrumental to achieving targets in goals related to income, poverty, water, education, energy, cities and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure open-government elements (e.g., citizen input, oversight, transparency of services) are integrated into sectoral SDG plans because they strengthen service quality and universal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, inclusive, participatory and transparent follow-up and review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2030 Agenda calls for follow-up and review processes that are 'open, inclusive, participatory and transparent for all people' and requires countries to conduct regular evaluations of progress and incorporate stakeholder input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design monitoring and review mechanisms to allow broad stakeholder access and contribution; track not only outcomes but the transparency and inclusiveness of review processes themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Open data, closely related to OGP transparency objectives, is increasingly recognized as important for development and for tracking progress on the SDGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize publishing high-quality, timely, and accessible data as part of SDG monitoring and OGP commitments; use open data to enable accountability and evidence-based decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt relevant commitments in OGP national action plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries should adopt OGP commitments in their national action plans that are relevant to implementing the SDGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate SDG priorities into concrete, timebound national OGP commitments (e.g., laws, institutional changes, data publication) and include them in action plans for accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote transparency and citizen participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments should take actions that promote transparency and enable meaningful citizen participation as a core element of SDG delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanisms for citizen engagement in policy design, service delivery, and oversight; avoid tokenistic consultation by ensuring contributions can influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate open government into SDG monitoring indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The OGP Declaration encourages integrating open government principles into the official indicators that will measure the Agenda’s progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate measures of transparency, participation, and institutional accountability into SDG indicators and reporting frameworks so progress on governance is visible and measurable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement with civil society in consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in deeper consultations with civil society when developing commitments and action plans (the UK took OGP review recommendations to engage more deeply with civil society).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure consultations to reach diverse CSOs, provide sufficient time and information, and demonstrate how input shaped commitments to avoid superficial or box-checking processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale up ambition in successive national action plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries should scale up commitments from their initial OGP action plans when updating them (examples: Brazil, South Africa, United States included more ambitious commitments in updated plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OGP peer review and lessons learned to increase the scope and depth of commitments over time; measure progress and raise ambition in subsequent cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cities and subnational governments in OGP efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of cities and subnational governments in OGP is promoted to open opportunities for local engagement and cross-learning on transparency and open government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend open-government reforms and SDG implementation strategies to local governments to improve service delivery and facilitate local-level accountability and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt or improve Freedom of Information (FOI) legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: A concrete OGP deliverable: in early OGP years, five countries passed new or improved Freedom of Information laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider FOI laws as a baseline legal reform to secure public access to information; measure enactment and effective implementation (access, responsiveness, appeal mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve transparency in public expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforms to improve transparency in public expenditures have been undertaken by several countries as OGP commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote fiscal transparency measures (budget publication, procurement data, open contracting) as essential to prevent leakage and improve service delivery tied to SDG outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political finance reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Political finance reforms (example: two countries enacted such reforms) are highlighted as part of accountability commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement measures to increase transparency and accountability in political financing to reduce corruption and strengthen democratic institutions supporting SDG progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen corporate accountability initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Some OGP commitments have aimed to strengthen corporate accountability (three countries developed new initiatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include private-sector transparency and accountability measures (e.g., disclosure, oversight, enforcement) where corporate activity affects SDG targets such as environment and land use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use open government to improve service delivery quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Open government (citizen input and oversight) is often an essential element of high-quality, universal service provision in sectors like education, infrastructure and health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design service-delivery reforms that embed opportunities for citizen feedback and oversight to enhance equity, quality, and reach of services crucial for SDG targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of research organizations in supporting OGP and SDGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research organizations (e.g., WRI) should help OGP member countries strengthen national commitments on climate and environment, engage subnational governments, and leverage global agreements on finance and climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and evidence organizations can provide technical assistance, data/tools, and policy advice to translate SDG priorities into concrete open-government commitments and monitor impact.
